stepNotes.1: Identified Rust rlib/cdylib outputs, four N-API JSON exports, wrapper packaging, and the absence of a runtime TypeScript importer.
stepNotes.2: Scoped risk to untrusted escape text and JSON crossing N-API; no filesystem, network, subprocess, or persistent-state capability exists in the crate.
stepNotes.3: Traced parser precedence, lifecycle transitions, viewport clamping, buffer normalization, checked diff access, and N-API error conversion.
stepNotes.4: Reviewed linear scans, per-scalar allocation, JSON copies, and the one-million-cell viewport ceiling without asserting an unmeasured regression.
stepNotes.5: Separated pure terminal-domain logic from thin N-API adapters and confirmed the current Zig/OpenTUI ownership boundary leaves this Rust addon dormant.
stepNotes.6: Found no unsafe blocks, debt markers, panic macros, or production unwrap calls; retained build registration prevents labeling the entire crate accidental dead code.
stepNotes.7: Mapped 24 Rust tests to parser, ANSI, buffer, lifecycle, and Critical SS3 risks; confirmed the audit-listed TypeScript tests cover different TUI modules.
stepNotes.8: Revalidated AUDIT-crate-terminal-001 as Critical stability, verified-fixed by UTF-8-width consumption and focused unknown-final regressions.
stepNotes.9: Recorded successful cargo test and clippy runs and produced the required independent Critical second-pass record.
